title: Robustness and Trade-offs for Code LLMs on Protected Code
abstract: arXiv:2609.04220v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Code large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used on software artifacts that may be intentionally obfuscated for intellectual-property protection, reverse-engineering resistance, or controlled access. In reverse engineering and security analysis, deobfuscation is commonly treated as the preprocessing step before downstream analysis or inference, yet its utility for code LLM pipelines has not been systematically validated across models and protection methods. We present an execution-based study of seven code LLMs on protected-code translation and completion, spanning source programs from C++, Go, Java, and JavaScript, five obfuscation methods, and three inference protocols: plain, obfuscated, and deobfuscated. Our results show that direct inference on obfuscated code often matches or exceeds inference on restored code. In this controlled benchmark, higher-capability models such as GPT-4.1 and Qwen3-Coder-30B retain about 90% Pass@1

translated_title: 面向受保护代码的代码大语言模型的鲁棒性与权衡
translated_abstract: 代码大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被应用于可能因知识产权保护、抗逆向工程或受控访问而被刻意混淆的软件制品上。在逆向工程与安全分析中，去混淆通常被视为下游分析或推理之前的预处理步骤，然而其在代码LLM流水线中的效用尚未在不同模型和保护方法间得到系统性验证。我们针对七个代码LLM在受保护代码的翻译与补全任务上开展了一项基于执行的实证研究，涵盖来自C++、Go、Java和JavaScript的源程序、五种混淆方法以及三种推理协议：原始代码、混淆代码和去混淆代码。我们的结果表明，直接对混淆代码进行推理的效果通常不亚于甚至优于对还原代码进行推理的效果。在此受控基准中，GPT-4.1和Qwen3-Coder-30B等更高能力的模型保留了约90%的Pass@1（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文通过涵盖4种语言、5种混淆方法和3种推理协议的基于执行的系统性研究，首次验证了代码LLM直接推理混淆代码的效果往往不亚于甚至优于先去混淆再推理，从而对去混淆作为预处理步骤的必要性提出了质疑。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first execution-based systematic study across 4 languages, 5 obfuscation methods, and 3 inference protocols, showing that code LLMs performing direct inference on obfuscated code often match or even outperform inference on deobfuscated code, thereby questioning the necessity of deobfuscation as a preprocessing step.
